Description: explicit — naming published tile schemas and their doc URLs
prompt: I'm writing style layers against an unfamiliar vector tile source and need to know the possible source-layer names. What are the major published vector tile schemas I should check, and where are their layer lists documented?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Thinking: We need to answer: major published vector tile schemas, their layer lists documentation URLs. Based on skill: OpenMapTiles, Shortbread, Protomaps. Possibly also MapLibre's own? Provide list with description and links. Also mention that TileJSON vector_layers can be used. Provide guidance. Below are the three **widely‑used, publicly‑documented vector‑tile schemas** that you’ll run into most often when you are writing style layers “against an unfamiliar vector tile source”. For each schema I give: | Schema | Who maintains it | Typical use‑case | Where the **authoritative layer list** lives (human‑readable page + machine‑readable hint) | |--------|------------------|------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | **OpenMapTiles** | OpenMapTiles community (open‑source, built on OpenStreetMap data) | Full‑featured world‑wide basemap, the de‑facto standard for “large‑scale” OSM‑derived vector tiles. | • Human‑readable layer list: (scroll to “Layers”)
• Machine‑readable (when a TileJSON is served) – the `vector_layers` array in the TileJSON (e.g. `https://free.tilehosting.com/data/v3.json?key=YOUR_KEY`). | | **Shortbread** | Shortbread‑tiles project (independent, minimal, interoperable spec) | Small, portable tilesets that aim to be schema‑agnostic and easy to implement in any language. | • Human‑readable layer list: → “Layer definitions” section (or directly )
• Machine‑readable: Shortbread TileJSON includes a `vector_layers` array; many hosted endpoints expose it (e.g. `https://tiles.shortbread.org/tiles.json`). | | **Protomaps** | Protomaps (PMTiles ecosystem) | Server‑less, flat‑file delivery of a lightweight basemap (often used with the `pmtiles://` protocol). | • Human‑readable layer list:
• Machine‑readable: Protomaps‑generated TileJSON (e.g. `https://example.com/tiles/planet.pmtiles?format=tilejson`) contains `vector_layers`. | --- ## How to use the list in practice 1. **Ask the provider for a TileJSON URL** (most tile servers – Martin, tileserver‑gl, PMTiles, etc. – expose one). ```json { "type": "vector", "url": "https://mytileserver.com/tileset.json" } ``` Open that URL in a browser or `curl`; the `vector_layers` array will give you the exact `source-layer` names and the fields each layer contains. 2. **If no TileJSON is available**, you have to guess the schema. Compare the tile URL’s domain or the documentation you received with the three schemas above. * Example: a URL like `https://tiles.openstreetmap.org/…` almost always means **OpenMapTiles**. * A URL that contains `shortbread` or `sb-` is likely the **Shortbread** schema. * A `pmtiles://` URL or a host that advertises “Protomaps basemap” points to the **Protomaps** schema. 3. **Validate the names** – once you think you know the schema, open its layer list page and copy the exact `source‑layer` strings into your style layers. ```json { "id": "road-lines", "type": "line", "source": "my-basemap", "source-layer": "transportation", // OpenMapTiles name "paint": { "line-color": "#777" } } ``` 4. **If you still get no output**, double‑check: * The TileJSON’s `minzoom`/`maxzoom` (hand‑wired `tiles` arrays default to `maxzoom:22`). * CORS headers on the tile server. * That the layer you are styling is actually a **vector** layer (raster sources have no `source‑layer`). --- ### Quick reference links | Schema | Layer list page | Example TileJSON (if you need a concrete file) | |--------|----------------|-----------------------------------------------| | OpenMapTiles | https://openmaptiles.org/schema/ | https://free.tilehosting.com/data/v3.json?key=YOUR_KEY | | Shortbread | https://shortbread-tiles.org/ (or https://shortbread-tiles.org/layers) | https://tiles.shortbread.org/tiles.json | | Protomaps | https://docs.protomaps.com/basemaps/layers | https://example.com/tiles/planet.pmtiles?format=tilejson | --- ### TL;DR checklist - **First step**: Look for a TileJSON `url`. If you have it, read `vector_layers` – that’s the definitive source‑layer list. - **No TileJSON?** → Guess the schema and consult the three pages above. - **Match the name exactly** (case‑sensitive, no extra spaces). A typo or a layer from a different schema yields a silent “nothing draws” symptom. - **After you have the names**, add your style layers *before* the first `symbol` layer (or use `map.addLayer(layer, firstSymbolId)`) so you don’t hide the basemap’s labels. With those three schemas and the TileJSON `vector_layers` field in hand, you should be able to wire any unfamiliar vector tile source to a working MapLibre style. Happy styling!
